title: QUIC RFC 9000 Disable Active Migration Preferred Address Exception
purpose: Describe the RFC 9000 Section 18.2 disable_active_migration transport-parameter floor and the preferred_address exception to that migration restriction.
design_summary: The transport-parameter codec represents disable_active_migration as the empty QUIC transport parameter with ID 0x0c and rejects non-empty values. Runtime peer transport-parameter commit maps a received disable_active_migration parameter into QuicConnectionTransportState.DisableActiveMigration. Active-path promotion then treats that flag as a policy gate for ordinary migration candidates while permitting a validated candidate path that matches the peer preferred_address transport parameter, preserving RFC 9000's explicit preferred-address exception.
data_and_state_considerations: The runtime keeps the disable-active-migration policy in transportFlags after peer transport parameters are committed. Candidate paths are still created and validated so address-validation state is not lost, but non-preferred candidates remain candidates while the active path stays on the handshake address. Preferred-address matching continues to use the parsed preferred_address IPv4 or IPv6 address and port.
edge_cases_and_constraints: disable_active_migration is encoded with an empty value and rejected if the value is non-empty.
Committing peer transport parameters with disable_active_migration sets both PeerTransportParametersCommitted and DisableActiveMigration runtime flags.
A validated non-preferred migration candidate does not promote while disable_active_migration is set.
A preferred_address candidate still waits for path validation before promotion.
A validated preferred_address candidate promotes even when disable_active_migration is set.
A port-only preferred_address transition remains eligible for the preferred-address exception.
risks: This slice is internal runtime proof and does not claim public migration APIs or hosted interop behavior.
The implementation remains single-active-path; multipath scheduling is out of scope.
The proof does not claim complete preferred_address field-shape closure for the broader S18P2 preferred-address tuple.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the bounded disable_active_migration and preferred_address exception requirements for S18P2. It does not claim max_ack_delay policy, initial data-limit parameters, the preferred_address field-shape family, public migration APIs, multipath, or hosted interop readiness.
